scores.reason: Measure type: post-load multi-sample OGTT insulin, C-peptide and glucose indices plus MR-spectroscopy liver fat (liver fat is not an insulin measure). One randomised trial (n=1105, 908 completers) tested phenotype-stratified lifestyle intensity, and intensified lifestyle was favoured in the high-risk group (difference CI -0.544 to -0.036). But the endpoint is post-challenge glucose (a surrogate), there is no replication, the phenotype is not insulin-only, the local text is a preprint, and no guideline mentions it. The cap is clarification 8: the measure stratified the programme, but measurement-guided care was never tested against unguided care; the alternative of 3 is not applied (clarification 9, surrogate endpoint).
sources: PMID 34531293 DOI 10.2337/db21-0526 (medRxiv preprint version, text read by keyword search per usecases-verified.md row 51)

scores.reason: Measure type: post-load. The phenotype combines secretion, sensitivity and liver fat, so the insulin contribution is not isolated. The row text does not report a comparison with glucose, HbA1c, BMI or a liver-fat score, and the multi-sample OGTT plus MRS burden is heavy. No reclassification or incremental data were found in the project files, so by clarification 19 mechanism alone gives at most 2; 1 chosen because no added value over simpler alternatives is shown.

scores.reason: Measure type: fasting-based (fasting insulin or HOMA-IR; one study used a mixed composite). TRIO-BD (n=45) enrolled only insulin-resistant patients, so it never tested selection by IR (entry criterion only, capped at 2 by clarification 8), and its main comparison was between converters and non-converters, not metformin against placebo. Lin 2015 (42 enrolled, 37 completed) is a small trial in which improvement in depression was associated with improvement in glucose metabolism only in patients with insulin resistance (an association of changes, not a treatment effect by subgroup). Neither was randomised by IR status, so I scored 1.

scores.reason: Measure type: post-load (INS-30). The DIETFITS randomised trial (n=609, 12 months) found no diet by INS-30 interaction (P=.47) and similar weight loss, so the available evidence is against a decision effect. Scored 0 as the evidence that the result changes the decision: none supports it, and the one trial tested and found no effect modification. The score refers to the insulin test, not to dietary treatment. Score 0 means no supporting evidence, not proof of absence: one null interaction test (P=.47) in 609 adults with a weight outcome only, not shown to be powered to exclude a modest effect.

scores.reason: Measure type: post-load (INS-30). With no interaction (P=.47) the measure does not separate responders, so it adds nothing over assigning either diet by preference. One trial, weight outcome only, so a modest-sized interaction cannot be excluded; confidence is medium.

Measure type: fasting-based (fasting insulin, HOMA; C-peptide in some cohorts). Cohorts (n=512, 527, 535) show association with recurrence or death, but the 512 cohort's recurrence association weakened after BMI adjustment (HR 1.7, 0.9 to 3.1) and one cohort found associations only in the first 5 years. Window-of-opportunity metformin (n=48) was small, MA.32 (n=3649) showed no clear dependence of insulin lowering on baseline insulin and did not test recurrence, and the PI3K finding is from mice (with an erratum). This is association and prognosis only, with no insulin-guided decision tested; 1 chosen because the cohort data do not address a decision (2 would be the pure observational band).

anchor_issues: Row 51 D2: a single stratified RCT on a surrogate endpoint with no guideline fits neither 2 (observational) nor 3 (guideline-backed). Chose 2; 3 is the alternative.
Row 53 D2/D8: a negative entry has no anchor for evidence against a decision effect. Chose 0 for both.
Row 54 D2: prognosis-only cohort evidence with no decision named; chose 1 (not 2) because D2 is evidence for decision impact. Row 54 D8 set to null (no comparator data).
Row 51: the exposure bundles insulin-based indices with MRS liver fat; D8 cannot isolate the insulin contribution.
